title: AuxiliarySimilarityNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of f=I.1; neither f nor the auxiliary function h=I.2 is assumed convex. The initial objective gap satisfies f(x0)-inf f ≤ Δ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Two separately budgeted oracles return exact gradients of f and h at arbitrary queried points. Replies are independent of history and seeds. All parameters, including L, δ, ρ, Δ and ε, are public; the functions are hidden.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each gradient query also returns the exact value of its corresponding function.

distinctive_assumptions.label: gradient_similarity
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient difference ∇f−∇h is globally δ-Lipschitz, with δ>0. Its magnitude is not bounded; this is a similarity condition between two exact oracles, not stochastic or pointwise relative error.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: f is C² with globally ρ-Lipschitz Hessian; h is differentiable with globally L-Lipschitz gradient. Parameters satisfy L≥0, ρ>0, Δ≥0 and ε>0.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return a single point x with ‖∇f(x)‖≤ε, using the norm itself, not its square.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The gradient-norm guarantee holds almost surely over the joint algorithm and oracle randomness, under fixed separate oracle budgets.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup augments smooth nonconvex stationarity with a separately queried auxiliary function whose gradient difference is Lipschitz, and measures the two oracle costs separately.

descriptionHtml:
Nonconvex Optimization with Auxiliary Similarity

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E, with a differentiable auxiliary function h:E→R. The objective is twice continuously differentiable with Lipschitz Hessian; both the auxiliary gradient and the gradient difference ∇f−∇h are Lipschitz. A given point x0∈E has bounded objective gap above the infimum. Two exact oracles return (f(x),∇f(x)) and (h(x),∇h(x)) at a query x∈E. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The parameters satisfy L≥0,δ>0,ρ>0,Δ≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives E, x0, L, δ, ρ, Δ, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Hessian regularity). The objective f is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable on E. Its Hessian, viewed as a linear operator from E to E, satisfies ∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤ρ∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 2 (Auxiliary smoothness and similarity). The auxiliary function h is Fréchet differentiable on E. For every x,y∈E, ∥∇h(x)−∇h(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,∥(∇f(x)−∇h(x))−(∇f(y)−∇h(y))∥≤δ∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Initial objective gap). The given point x0 satisfies f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ,x∈E.

Both oracles accept queries at any point of E, and their calls are counted separately. After the allotted calls, the required accuracy is ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤εP-a.s.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

namespace LongTails.Setups.AuxiliarySimilarityNonconvex

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  x0 : E
  L : ℝ
  δ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 2
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := (p.E → ℝ) × (p.E → ℝ)
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := ℝ × p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 ≤ p.L ∧ 0 < p.δ ∧ 0 < p.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I O :=
    ContDiff ℝ 2 I.1 ∧ Differentiable ℝ I.2 ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient I.1) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient I.1) y‖ ≤ p.ρ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖(gradient I.1 x - gradient I.2 x) - (gradient I.1 y - gradient I.2 y)‖ ≤
      p.δ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient I.2 x - gradient I.2 y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x, I.1 p.x0 - I.1 x ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (0, x) seed = (I.1 x, gradient I.1 x)) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (1, x) seed = (I.2 x, gradient I.2 x))
  successful p I output P :=
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), ‖gradient I.1 (output ω)‖ ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.AuxiliarySimilarityNonconvex
